doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: De De's birth and learning trumpet from Kid Rene
summary: De De gives his 1904 birth in New Orleans, says no one in his family played, and tells how a cousin's old trumpet, lessons from Kid Rene and reading lessons from an older teacher led to his own seven-piece band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: D.D., you might tell a little bit when you were... What was your birth date, how we think of it, so we'll be sure to get that. February 18th, 1904. 1904. Where were you born? New Orleans, right here. Do you remember the street? I mean, you wouldn't remember, but I mean they told you. Which street you...
St. Anne... No, let me get straight. I think it's Rushbrave. Rushbrave... What was it called? Old Indian Market.
Oh, yes.
Back there.
Back there.
Yeah, that's near Iberville somewhere in the city.
Were your folks musical?
No, none in the family.
Your father or mother didn't play or sing anything much? No, they played at all.

None of them did any musical, not at all. I just, you know, I liked it by hearing bands playing, you know. Yeah. I'd be in the take and take... In other words, I had a cousin, she was trying to play in the girl band. Her name was Leliska at the time. I was about seventeen then at the time. And she gave me an old trumpet and I just began to play by ear. And finally, I heard of a teacher, which was Kid Rene, he's also deceased.
Oh, yes.

Yeah. And I had my first few lessons from him. And then I left him and went and learnt more my reading, like the music part, from my shallow knee. He was an old mail carrier at the time. He was in his sixties during the time, he and I did. Yeah.
Where did he live?

He lived at St. Claude between Duvain and St. Philip at the time. And he was the leader of one of the old onward bands. Best band from years back, putting in about eighteen hundred something. Way back.
Way back.
Way back. They taught me. And from there on, well, I organized a seven piece band.
Had you played any instrument before you took up some of them?
No, no, no, no, none at all.
Any even little whistles or guitar or anything? No, just taking a liking to the trumpet.
Just taking a liking to the trumpet. By being given to me, you see. That's what she said.
